_about: The Models tab of the hangar page (tools/hangar.html): every render Ryan judges, by chassis. A round adds its pictures under docs/hangar/renders/<chassis>/, moves the previous 'images' to 'before' with a summary, and writes 'when' and 'note'; then the page is republished with the new files (tools/hangar_data.py prints the files map). 'classes' is the silhouette classes section, a list of blocks shown in order.

classes.title: Silhouette classes
classes.plate: What a swapped component wears at a gun mount · the rule settled 30 September

blocks.note: Hardpoints are gun mounts. A weapon, or equipment that can look like one (a shield projector, a buff coil), wears its class at the next mount in the die's order, in its own maker's metal; armour panels and vents take a die entry and no mount, since they are applied to the whole machine. Five classes: barrel, twin barrel, rack, blade (katar-style, punching forward) and dish. A machine with more hardpoints than stock guns carries bare mount pads. Shown: a Minerva barrel, a Wainwright & Sutler rack, a Kestrel dish, an Arsenal blade.

Four refits rendered with RIFTGATE_FIT: the Honey Badger with a W&S Lance on the wrist, a Heat Sink (which shows nowhere), an Arsenal Blazethrower on the left pauldron and a Kestrel Deflector's dish on the right; the Clydesdale with an Arc Projector in place of the Lance and, on its bare mounts, a Missile Rack, Soulcutter Talons and an Overcharge Coil; the Sparrowhawk with Soulcutter Talons as a wing blade and Meteor Artillery on the other tip; the Wild Boar with a Plasma Carbine and a Blazethrower on its rear quarters.

Ryan, 2 November: “Can't we just model different shapes as options, as needed?” A variant is a class in another form, modelled for the mounts its standard shape does not fit and named for its form, so any hardpoint may take it; a hardpoint declares, for each class, the variant it wears and its scale there, and every other hardpoint wears the class itself at its own scale. The first is the round launcher, for a round port or a pod's nose (the Polar Bear's ports, the Goshawk's pods), its face the square rack's missile tile one tube at a time. Shown in Minerva's and Wainwright & Sutler's metal; Classes on the Models tab shows it alone.

badger.note: Ryan's go, 28 October: since the stock pass its stock is the Rivet Gun alone, on the deck's ring as its class, the gimbals bare (the Canopy and the Coolant Jacket show nowhere); the missile box and the gimbals' autoguns went with the old stock.

before.summary: Before: twelfth round, third pass, 6 October (the missile box and the gimbals' autoguns)

clydesdale.note: Ryan's go, 28 October: the stations keep their kinds and each mount its stock part in order: the Maxigun as its class on the left turret where the autoguns were, the cheek bracket's left mount the Incendiary Shells' rack, the right bare; the lance, the mortar, the howitzer and the deck rack (the Airburst Shell's) as before. Since 31 October its stock Incendiary Shells wear a burn weapon's fire over their rack, glowing shells dim at rest and flaring as they fire.

before.summary: Before: the fifteenth notes, 6 October (the second pair of autoguns and the bare cheeks)

sparrowhawk.note: Ryan, 29 October, the second notes: each tooth round a driver's inlet runs its back face aft as a strake, tapering down the drum until it meets it. The rest as the first notes left it: each Pinion Driver a ramjet-gun, a chrome drum with a lit ring tapering to a lit exhaust, the barrel out of the inlet's centre; two shots at half, one from each tip.

before.summary: Before: the first notes of 29 October (the teeth a ring round the lip)

baboon.note: Ryan's go, 28 October: every station keeps its kind, the pins renumbered to the stock's order and each part its class: the shoulders' elevating mounts carry the Halo Shield's dish (left) and the Ankle Mortar's rack (right) where the Umbra Projectors rode; the fists' outer sides the Twin Autoguns (right) and the Rivet Gun (left) where the Pulse Repeaters were; the right fist's top the Laser Carbine where the Zenith Emitter was; the left fist's top bare.

before.summary: Before: fourth round, 30 September (the Umbra Projectors, the Pulse Repeaters and the Zenith Emitter)

polar_bear.note: Ryan, 2 November: “what happens if they get swapped out, like putting a missile rack on the armadillo gun port”, then “maybe some hardpoints want circular missile racks, that fixes the armadillo” and “Hardpoint just needs to declare shape (if offered) and scaling”. A class fitted in a port now wears the port's own fit: a rack is the round launcher (a drum with seven tubes, the square rack's missile tile one tube at a time), and every class is sized to pass the port's bore whole, so it rises out of the port as the guns do and sinks under the iris when the shell seals; a rack had been a square box half again as wide as the port, jammed in its mouth. The fore ports are wider (11 across, from 9) and a little lower, so a launcher or a dish fitted there reads; stock, they are bare as before. The shots: the stock (front, rear, side, sealed, venting from behind and from the front), then a round launcher in every port, then a launcher, the Twin Autoguns, a barrel and a dish. Fit any mount on the Models tab to try the rest.

before.summary: Before: the tenth notes of 30 October (every class one size in the ports, the fore ports 9 across)

prairie_dog.note: Ryan's go, 28 October: the projector on the rear-left corner is the stock's Halo Shield as its class, a dish facing forward; the launcher there went with the old stock. The Flakshot Repeater and the turret as before.

before.summary: Before: 9 October, sixth pass (the rear-left launcher)

dingo.note: Ryan's go of 2 November: the nose mounts sat inside the raked nose, which buried a fitted dish and half sank a rack. Each now stands on a low pedestal on the nose ahead of the visor, the stock's Twin Autoguns on the left one, so whatever is fitted stands clear. The shots: the stock from the front and behind, two racks, then a dish and a blade.

before.summary: Before: Ryan's glow notes, 31 October (the nose mounts inside the nose)

goshawk.note: Ryan's go of 2 November: a swap had taken a pod with its gun and hung the class under the wing, where the game's camera lost the inner pair. The pods are airframe now and stay; each mount is its pod's nose, so a fitted class rides ahead of the wing, a rack as the round launcher (a rocket pod), the wide classes a little smaller so they sit on a pod. The stock looks as before. The shots: the stock from the front and behind, a round launcher on every pod, then the Twin Autoguns, a launcher, a dish and a barrel.

before.summary: Before: the stock rebuild, 28 October (each pod part of its gun)

nemesis.note: Hot at rest, really hot as it acts (Ryan, 31 October: "not burn crazy hot all the time. Just like, hot, then really hot"): the chest furnace and the condenser on its back smoulder always and flare in its fierce acts, the vent toned down ("still too much"). The last picture is the fist pound's blow.

ammit.note: The vent at its tail, the condenser's twin, always lit in the furnace's orange and flaring in its fierce acts (Ryan, 31 October: "Ammit vents don't seem to be glowing"; the glow had gone to the throat vent under the jaw, which no camera sees). The last picture is the threat.

stingray.note: A lit lining round the fans' blades and the floor under them in one even orange (Ryan, 31 October: "Anything to be done about the stingray fans?"): the downwash blows under the wing, where no camera looks, so the duct's walls carry the heat; the glow tile's hot centre had read yellow. The last picture is the thrusters' surge.

puffin.note: The repulsors are pucks standing proud of the plates (Ryan, 31 October: "if the solution is to give them geometry, then go ahead"), in one even orange, always on as it hovers; a flat disc's halo stood off it as a copy, and the engine tile's metal rim flared white. The last picture is the amplify.

funnel_web.note: Ryan's go, 28 October: since the stock pass its fourth stock piece is a Canopy, which shows nowhere, so the right pod's mount is bare; the deflector's dish there went with the old stock. The model is otherwise the good-to-go of 20 October.

before.summary: Before: fourth cut, 19 October; revised on Ryan's fifth to eleventh notes, 19 and 20 October, and good to go on the eleventh (the deflector's dish on the right pod)

Earlier: funnel-web, a moment of the creep, side on

skua.note: The round hinges at the wings' wrists gone (Ryan, 31 October: "they look cheap").

before.summary: Before: Second round, the jaeger; its run a flown circle, 28 October

needletail.note: Claude's first cut, 23 October (Ryan: models for every chassis ready to build, their silhouettes apart from the Kestrel roster's). From above, the view the player reads, the roster is the Kite's dart on forward-swept wings with a V tail, the Buzzard's tailless plank, the Puffin's blunt hull on stubs, and the Lammergeier's two wing pairs to come. The Needletail is a needle of a fuselage on a short straight stub wing with a big booster nacelle on each tip, standing upright at rest so it hovers on them, exhausts down, where the Buzzard's nacelles tilt on the shoulders of a broad-winged airframe; a long thin tail ending in a dark needle with an X of small fins; a wide spotter's canopy; the Fovea Designator a sensor ball on a mast behind it, turning and nodding, its lens lit as it paints. Its acts: the transition to level flight and back, a sidestep, designating, backpedalling on its nacelles tipped back. On the move its nacelles tilt level as it gathers speed and come upright as it slows. Ryan's to judge running.

storm_petrel.note: The Riot Field, its emitters, rails, strips, fin tips and the arch, in the shield's blue (Ryan, 31 October), the arch wearing the halo; St. Elmo's fire banked to an electric blue ("a tinge of something other than white"). The last picture is the field up.

before.summary: Before: The swap, the field lit, the arch sleeved, 28 October

images.alt: Earlier: storm_petrel, St. Elmo's fire in the port

giant_petrel.note: Claude's first cut, 23 October (Ryan: models for every chassis ready to build, their silhouettes apart from the Kestrel roster's). From above, the view the player reads, the roster is the Kite's dart on forward-swept wings with a V tail, the Buzzard's tailless plank, the Puffin's blunt hull on stubs, and the Lammergeier's two wing pairs to come. The Giant Petrel is after the Lun: a long flying-boat hull, the longest thing Kestrel builds; eight boosters in two banks of four on canards over the bow (the Immelmann Booster), pitching to blow under the wings; short cobalt wings low on the hull with float pontoons and endplates; a tall T-tail; the Spindrift Salvo's three pairs of tubes along the spine on a plinth that elevates, each back-blast lit; the Reheat Uplink's dish behind the cockpit; two turrets. Its acts: the salvo, the Immelmann, the uplink, a traverse. On the move it runs heavy and slow, nose a touch up. Ryan's to judge running.

images.alt: giant petrel, the salvo, its battery raised

lammergeier.when: First model, the flying wing, the launcher nacelles on the skin, 28 October.
lammergeier.note: The chrome chevron drawn as a hovercraft for the Giant Petrel (the third round, docs/looks/kestrel_giant.png), given to the Lammergeier airborne on Ryan's thought of 27 October ("looks good but careful on the weapon mount placement so they don't clip"): a deeper centre body with the canopy forward and the bomb bay under it on a lit seam, four booster drums across the trailing edge, the Syrinx Drone's tubes in the leading edge's roots, the Lorentz Contractor's dish on a dorsal pylon, the mounts on the wing in the bays between the drums. The last picture is the lay_mines act. 28 October: the drone tubes sit in a pod on each leading-edge root, its face raked with the edge, so the wing's skin no longer shows inside them (Ryan's note). His second notes (the pods did not work as meant): each is now a nacelle on the leading-edge root that carries the wing's full thickness forward to a blunt raked face, top and bottom, the two tubes let into the face. His third (the box was fine; the hull-coloured tube ends clipping through its raked face were the mistake): each tube's mouth follows the face's rake, a touch proud of it, in the nacelle's dark. His fourth: the tubes bored twelve deep (an end cap is no tube). His fifth (the mouths read as end caps, not inset): each mouth is a hole cut through the face plate, the bore flush in it in the lighter plate so its far wall catches the light. His sixth (the open bores showed the wing's skin again, which the caps had hidden: the skin climbs over the bore's depth): the nacelle rides on the wing's upper skin, its underside following the skin's rise from the edge, the tubes above the skin the whole way. His seventh: the bores dark, not the hull's light plate. Since 31 October its stock Incendiary Shells wear a burn weapon's fire over their rack, glowing shells dim at rest and flaring as they fire.
